about.title: Personal Injury Help in Fillmore, California
about.longDescription: Fillmore sits along Rt 126, where local traffic on Ventura Street and A Street mixes with drivers passing through the Santa Clara River Valley. In the most recent full year on record, Fillmore saw 58 injury collisions, with 90 people hurt and 2 lives lost — public-record counts that reflect how much can happen on even a small town's streets. Many of these crashes cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when weekend traffic builds along the SR-126 corridor. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel like a full-time job on top of recovering. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm — that connects injured people in Fillmore with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We don't practice law or handle your case ourselves; we simply help you get in front of someone who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, without cost or obligation to you.

items.title: A Filing Deadline That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require action in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a crash, you can still pursue compensation — it's simply reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering Claims
items.desc: For ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and emotional distress, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of a settlement or award — never out of pocket up front.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Fillmore?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. If a government entity, like a city or county vehicle, was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do injury crashes tend to cluster in Fillmore?
items.answer: Public crash records show that collisions in Fillmore concentrate along corridors like Rt 126, Ventura Street, and A Street, with a noticeable rise in reports on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your total recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Is there a cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney — we are not a law firm and don't charge you anything to make that connection.

items.question: Do I have to pay the attorney upfront?
items.answer: Attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront legal fee to worry about while you focus on recovering.
